chunks: And We brought the people of Israel across the sea, but the Pharaoh and his army pursued them wickedly and maliciously till he was on the point of drowning, and he said: 'I believe that there is no god but He in whom the people of Israel believe, and I submit to Him.'

key_terms.بَغْياً وَعَدْواً: Wickedly and maliciously / with hostility and aggression

ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh say when death overtook him after pursuing the Children of Israel?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the contrast between Pharaoh's ultimate submission (al-Islam) and his earlier arrogance, noting that while his faith was accepted, it was too late to save him from destruction due to his prior tyranny. The narrative serves as a profound lesson on the efficacy of deathbed repentance, a concept frequently discussed by Shia scholars regarding the conditions for divine mercy. This event is often cited to illustrate the transient nature of worldly power when contrasted with the enduring truth of Tawhid.
